environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; one client socket per composition, strict-token peer with a monotonic SEQ counter echoed into the body, hex-exact client capture

findings.description: `GET /api%2fexec%20?cmd=id` immediately followed by `GET /api/hello.txt` on one socket. `request()` re-runs for the follower and overwrites `c.upfd`/`c.upsend` while the first connection is still in flight, so the first request's buffer is replaced before it is drained; `:64` also hardcodes `close=true` on every proxied branch, so the dropped response had no frame to land in. Static-first and nonexec-first both lose request 1, so it is not exec-specific.
findings.title: The second pipelined request overwrites the live upstream buffer, so the first request is silently dropped and its exec never runs

limitations: Intra-connection only; no cross-client leak was found
Needs an attacker-influenced upstream and a pipelining client
All RCE is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Read the release source from the tag
